minutes.headline: Water commissioners directed the clerk-treasurer to go for the final 20-year bond in February for the Massapoag main project.
minutes.summary: Commissioners reviewed the near-complete water main replacement and choices for financing it (another temporary note versus going to bond now, 20 versus 27 years). They moved to charge the clerk-treasurer to pursue the final 20-year bond in February. They also heard worsening PFAS results at Lancaster Ave wells, discussed fixing the old dump truck and pricing a wheeled excavator, and approved prior minutes.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked about the rubber-tire excavator replacing the backhoe, the Kings pilot/treatment process and disposal of PFAS-contaminated hardness waste, in-house digging, the Rolling Acres phasing, and why own funds rather than borrowed money would cover overruns.
A resident asked about borrowing costs and rates for the short-term and long-term options, whether there is a prepayment penalty, and whether interest rates will drop.

votes.motion: Charge the clerk-treasurer to move forward with the final bond in February for 20 years to close out financing of the Massapoag water main replacement.

budget_items.topic: Temporary borrowing for water main project
budget_items.what_was_said: Temporary borrowing comes due in February; options were another temporary round until July or going to final bond now.
Total repayment over 20 years was presented, with the per-quarter customer charge; 27 years would cost much more in total but only slightly less per customer.
The current charge brings in more per year than the loan needs, giving some cushion; the charge is dedicated to this project.
Project is roughly on budget with some spring work to come; modest overruns could be covered from existing funds.
Amounts under a threshold can be reallocated by the chair to a similar water project; larger amounts need a special meeting.
Possible Mass DOT paving requirement estimated as a modest extra cost that could be paid from existing funds.
A new dump body was priced far above the repair option; board favored repairing the truck from the maintenance/special line or truck account.
State-bid prices were obtained for wheeled excavators to replace the old backhoe; no purchase decided.
Pilot delayed for lack of well run time; the well will run continuously, costing only electricity.
Estimated rates were discussed for 20 and 27 years, with total interest over the term noted.

decisions.decision: Board consensus to go to bond now rather than another temporary round, and to use 20 years rather than 27, so rating work with S&P Global can start.
Agreed to repair the dump truck's body using the maintenance/special line and truck account rather than buy a new truck.
Agreed a workshop and cost comparison of in-house versus contracted water main work (e.g. Rolling Acres) is needed before buying equipment.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners moved to charge the clerk-treasurer with pursuing a final 20-year bond in February for the Massapoag water main replacement; the recorded outcome of the vote was not audible.
The board reached consensus to go to bond now rather than take another temporary note, and to use 20 years rather than 27, so rating work with S&P Global can begin.
Commissioners agreed to repair the old dump truck from the maintenance/special line or truck account rather than buy a new one.
On equipment, the board agreed a workshop and cost comparison of in-house versus contracted water main work is needed before buying a wheeled excavator.
The board heard PFAS results at the Lancaster Ave wells and a delay in Kings pilot testing for lack of well run time.

why_it_matters: The financing choice sets how long customers pay for the Massapoag main replacement through the dedicated per-connection quarterly charge, and the total interest paid over the term.

PFAS results at the Lancaster Ave wells and the pending treatment pilot point to future treatment costs, and the excavator question to a possible equipment purchase, that water customers may be asked to fund.
